body.title: getValidatedQuery should account for ambiguous data
body.body:
### Describe the feature

## Premise

readQuery() as it is currently only works if you either

1. have extremely simple data - basically exclusively strings.
2. make a custom schema with coercing (assuming the validation library supports everything needed) for every API endpoint, not really being able to reuse existing schemas
3. send all data as body payload (this wouldn't be a problem if GET and DELETE were allowed to have bodies)
4. send all data as stringified JSON
5. or (like me) make a shim that tries its best at adjusting the data to better fit a schema

none of these options are particularly enticing, so (imo) there should be a system to somehow fix this in h3.

## My shim/workaround

without posting code, I basically crawl through the zod type definition alongside the passed data and adjust the data where it can't be unambiguously represented by query parameters.

I'm not sure how viable this is for h3 considering it's supposed to be somewhat validator-agnostic… But then again, having this feature for a limited amount of libraries would be better than having it for none at all.

## Additional notes

zod has already declined to implement a version of this on their side: https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/issues/2873

### Additional information

- [ ] Would you be willing to help implement this feature?

body.title: fix(mime): add .mjs and .cjs to COMMON_MIME_TYPES
body.body:
`.mjs` (ES module) and `.cjs` (CommonJS module) files are absent from `COMMON_MIME_TYPES`. When `serveStatic` serves a `.mjs` file, `getType` returns `undefined` and no `Content-Type` header is set.

Browsers enforce strict MIME checking for `<script type="module">` — a missing content-type causes a network error and the module fails to load entirely.

The fix adds both extensions mapped to `"text/javascript"`, consistent with `.js` and with [RFC 9239](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9239).

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * `.mjs` and `.cjs` files are now identified as JavaScript files.

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

body.title: fix(cookie): size cookie chunks by their encoded length
body.body:
## Summary

`setChunkedCookie` splits the raw value every `chunkMaxLength` (default 4000) characters. Each chunk is then percent-encoded by `setCookie` (`encodeURIComponent` by default), and that encoding makes it longer: `"`, `{`, `:`, `,` and spaces become 3 bytes, and non-ASCII characters become 6–12 bytes. So the stored chunks can be far larger than the ~4KB the chunking is meant to stay under.

```ts
setChunkedCookie(event, "cart", JSON.stringify(cart)); // 7501 characters
// Set-Cookie: cart=__chunked__2
// Set-Cookie: cart.1=… (9195 bytes)
// Set-Cookie: cart.2=… (7932 bytes)
```

Browsers drop cookies over 4096 bytes, so the chunks never come back. On the next request `getChunkedCookie` sees `__chunked__2` with the chunks missing and returns `undefined`. The data is lost without any error.

A second failure in the same slicing: `value.slice()` cuts at UTF-16 indexes, so a chunk boundary can split a surrogate pair (an emoji, for example). `encodeURIComponent` then throws `URIError: URI malformed`, and the handler fails with a 500.

Session cookies aren't affected: the sealed value is URL-safe ASCII. It hits apps that put JSON or user text into chunked cookies.

## Fix

A new internal helper, `splitCookieValue`, splits the value on code point boundaries, so a surrogate pair is never split. Each chunk is the longest run whose encoded form, using the same `encode` as `setCookie` (`options.encode` or `encodeURIComponent`), fits in `chunkMaxLength`. The helper measures whole candidate chunks (gallop, then bisect), so custom encoders like base64 whose length isn't additive per character are sized correctly too. A code point that can't fit even alone throws before any header is written. For values that don't grow when encoded (such as sealed sessions), the chunks are exactly the same as before, so all existing chunk snapshots are unchanged. The chunk-count cap still applies, and the helper stops as soon as it's exceeded.

## Test plan

- [x] New tests in `test/cookies.test.ts` (web and node, both setups):
  - `keeps every encoded chunk within chunkMaxLength and readable`: a 2771-character JSON value (7453 bytes encoded). Every `Set-Cookie` value is ≤ 4000 bytes, and `getChunkedCookie` reads back the original.
  - `does not split a surrogate pair across chunks`: `"12345678901😀abc"` with `chunkMaxLength: 12` round-trips.
  - `sizes chunks for a custom encoder by the whole encoded chunk`: a `btoa` encoder with budget 40 gives 4 chunks of 30 characters, which round-trip.
  - `throws when a single character cannot fit in chunkMaxLength`
  - on `main` (62c2632): 16 failures (`expected 7453 to be less than or equal to 4000`, `URIError: URI malformed` → 500, …)
  - with this change: `test/cookies.test.ts` and `test/session.test.ts` 192/192
- [x] Full `vitest run` (node 24): 2872 passed, 66 skipped
- [x] `oxlint .`, `oxfmt --check .`, `tsc --noEmit`, `obuild` and `git diff --check` are clean

This bug was found and fixed by an AI agent (breken-ai) and verified with the red/green tests above.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Chunked cookies now respect size limits based on their encoded representation, including when values contain multibyte characters.
  * Character pairs remain intact across chunks, and chunk sizes account for the complete output of custom encoders.
  * If a single character cannot fit within the encoded size limit, the operation returns an HTTP 500 error without writing response headers.
  * The existing 100-chunk limit remains in place.
